name: Maoism–Third Worldism
summary: Maoism–Third Worldism combines Marxism-Leninism-Maoism with a dependency-theory view that the First World is a parasitic exploiter bloc whose workers form a labor aristocracy bought off with surplus extracted from the Third World. It holds that the real revolutionary proletariat lies in Asia, Africa and Latin America and that global people's war by oppressed nations is the path to communism, with the First World's role being mainly to be defeated or to repay its debt.
scope: The Maoist Internationalist Movement (MIM, 1983-2000s) and MIM (Prisons) as the best-documented organized current, plus Lin Biao's 1965 'Long Live the Victory of People's War!' as the shared precursor text. Excludes ordinary Marxism-Leninism-Maoism that treats First World workers as exploited, and non-Marxist Third Worldism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: MIM works for Third World proletarian welfare and treats state-provided services as part of socialist construction; an MLM adherent backs universal public health care, though MIM texts here do not address it directly.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: MIM argues First World wages are already bribes funded by Third World surplus, so raising them further deepens the labor aristocracy; adherent would not prioritise it (inferred).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: MIM Theory defends the Marxist account of exploitation and capitalist profit; markets are the mechanism of imperialist extraction.

public-ownership.rationale: Communist programme of socialised means of production; MIM upholds socialist state ownership as in Maoist China.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redistribution from capitalists is welcome, but MIM sees First World taxation as reformist and aimed at transfers within the exploiter nations (inferred).

unions-good.rationale: MIM holds that First World unions represent a worker-elite sharing in imperialist profits and cites strikes as showing white working class alliance with monopoly capital.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production is the basis of bourgeois exploitation in the MIM account.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents see regulation as reformist tinkering with imperialism, neither opposing nor desiring it; no direct statement.

cut-welfare.rationale: First World welfare is regarded as part of the bribe to the labor aristocracy, yet cutting it serves capital; adherents would not endorse cuts (inferred).

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist collective ownership is core, but MIM holds First World workers are not exploited, so a worker-run enterprise is not the route.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents see state surveillance as a tool of the imperialist state against oppressed nations and prisoners; inferred from MIM Prisons' position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: MIM and Maoism historically oppose drug use as bourgeois decay, yet MIM Prisons critiques the prison system; split and uncertain (inferred).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No stated position; MIM opposes white-nation chauvinism but is itself prone to be targeted by speech laws of an imperialist state.

strong-leader.rationale: Maoism stresses mass line and party leadership rather than a single bypassing leader; mildly negative by inference.

state-harmful.rationale: MIM holds the state is an instrument of class rule that must be seized, not simply abolished in the short term, and supports a socialist state.

limit-guns.rationale: MIM says power grows from armed struggle and the public seizing power by arms, so would not support restricting gun ownership by the imperialist state.

empower-police-military.rationale: The imperialist state apparatus including prisons and police is the enemy of oppressed nations in MIM's analysis.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Maoist tradition regards prostitution as exploitation to be eliminated; MIM texts do not address it directly (inferred).

decide-locally.rationale: Maoism combines mass line with democratic centralism; there is no stated preference on locality versus national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: MIM Prisons serves prisoners as oppressed-nation victims of a system, so favours rehabilitation over punishment, though sees real change only after revolution.

traditional-family.rationale: Maoist tradition opposes feudal patriarchal family structures; MIM aims to end oppression of genders.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Maoists are historically split on this and MIM texts here give no stance.

abortion-legal.rationale: MIM aims to end gender oppression, which suggests support for abortion access; no direct statement in the sources read.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxist materialism and Maoist tradition oppose religion's public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: MIM centres national oppression within imperialist borders and demands payment of the debt owed to oppressed nations.

gender-social-construct.rationale: MIM's statement of purpose targets gender oppression; it says race is made up, and likely treats gender roles similarly (inferred).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a priority; MIM identifies as internationalist world citizens, although supporting oppressed nations' culture.

gradual-change.rationale: People's war and armed struggle are the stated path; reformist gradualism is condemned as revisionism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: MIM argues borders are a device to keep labor markets separate and to preserve First World wage privileges; does not endorse restriction though objects that immigration is not itself a solution.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: UN and similar bodies are viewed as dominated by imperialist powers; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Delinking Third World economies from the First World and ending unequal exchange is central.

nation-first.rationale: MIM is internationalist and calls members world citizens, rejecting the First World nation's interests; yet supports oppressed nations' self-determination.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Lin Biao treats US-led intervention as imperialist aggression to be defeated by people's war.

open-borders.rationale: MIM says closed borders segment labor markets, yet argues open borders under imperialism would not help the oppressed; ambivalent.

limit-growth.rationale: No stated position; Maoism favours economic development in the Third World and is not degrowth-oriented (inferred).

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No direct statement; adherents blame imperialism for ecological harm and favour state action (inferred).

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Maoism holds social revolution, not technology, solves problems; no direct statement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No direct statement; Maoist China built nuclear weapons but energy stance is unaddressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Armed revolution through people's war is the central strategy.

experts-over-public.rationale: Mao's mass line stresses learning from masses over expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Maoist China's planned economy and the socialist state are endorsed as superior to capitalism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Maoism tends to oppose market socialism as a road to capitalist restoration, which MIM highlights in the Soviet and Chinese cases.

land-value-tax.rationale: A Georgist single tax is reformist; adherents would find it irrelevant to ending exploitation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Adherents oppose inherited class privilege, but regard tax reform as secondary.

basic-income.rationale: Seen as First World bribe to the labor aristocracy from imperialist super-profits, though not directly addressed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Self-reliance and delinking of Third World economies from the imperialist system implies protective measures for them; as a stance for the First World it is irrelevant.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Socialist state planning directs investment; Maoist China as the model.

widespread-small-property.rationale: MIM treats petty bourgeoisie as an intermediate class and seeks collective ownership rather than dispersed small property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ultimate communist goal of ending classes and wage relations, while stressing this lies far in the future.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A market-anarchist demand opposed to socialist planning and state control of finance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: MIM sees First World class collaboration as the labor aristocracy's alliance with capital and rejects it.

one-party-rule.rationale: MIM upholds dictatorship of the proletariat under a communist party and the Cultural Revolution.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anti-feudal, anti-hereditary rule is basic to Maoism.

democracy-best.rationale: Maoists reject bourgeois parliamentary democracy in favour of new democracy and proletarian dictatorship.

direct-votes.rationale: No direct stance; mass line preferred over referenda or parliaments.

workers-councils.rationale: Maoism favours party-led people's democracy, and MIM doubts First World workers' revolutionary role; mixed.

right-to-secede.rationale: MIM supports self-determination of all nations and peoples, including oppressed nations within the US.

natural-rulers.rationale: Maoist egalitarian thought rejects inherited or natural fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lin Biao endorses Mao's principle that seizing power by armed force and settling the issue by war is 'the central task and the highest form of revolution'.

war-builds-character.rationale: Wars of national liberation are endorsed but glorifying war itself is not a Maoist claim; MIM also stresses anti-militarism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Materialist, secularist tradition; no religion in state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: As a Marxist-Leninist-Maoist tendency it grounds law in class rule and materialism; no source discusses scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Contradicts the state as class instrument and socialist public ownership.

military-superiority.rationale: First World military superiority is imperialism; adherents want imperialist armies defeated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: MIM defines nation by land, language, economy and culture, not ethnicity, and calls race a made-up idea.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle as motor of history is core Marxism, held by MIM.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Adherents want an end to oppression of classes, genders and nations, and equality eventually; Maoism, however, tolerates unequal wages in the interim.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: MIM backs self-determination of oppressed nations, including indigenous peoples within settler states.

colonial-reparations.rationale: MIM states that imperialists and First World workers owe a debt to Third World peoples that it intends to see paid.

civilizational-union.rationale: Maoism-Third Worldism organises by class and imperialist oppression, not civilisation or religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Communist ethics reject self-interest as a moral guide.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mixed in Maoist tradition.

limit-population.rationale: Maoist China first resisted and then adopted population control; adherents not clearly aligned.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Maoism seeks industrial development of the Third World and sees capitalism, not industry, as the problem.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources read are silent on technological acceleration; Maoist tradition mixes industrialisation with distrust of disruption, so adherents are split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred: not a concern and viewed as First World privilege.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: mass line and party leadership instead.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: MIM Prisons works against state surveillance, but no stated stance.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revolution transforms society; Maoism is opposed to restoring pre-revolutionary order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Ideological line is held to decide outcomes in Maoism; pragmatic neutrality is rejected.

direct-action.rationale: Armed struggle versus parliaments is central, though a party leads, not spontaneous action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Maoists see violent means as the necessary route to a communist society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The tendency seeks socialist industrial development of the Third World; none of the sources entertains a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's communist goal, with Maoist emphasis on narrowing mental/manual gaps, but not a short-term aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist end-state formula, accepted as a long-term goal.

production-for-use.rationale: Core communist principle in contrast with capitalist profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: MIM defines exploitation as appropriation of surplus labour in profits.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: MIM explicitly holds that after the proletariat seizes power the dictatorship continues, and upholds the Cultural Revolution.

collective-farming.rationale: Maoist China's collectivisation is upheld; the sources read here do not detail it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lin Biao calls imperialism and class exploitation the roots of war; MIM says imperialists will wage war before ending oppression.

taxation-theft.rationale: A libertarian claim contradicting socialist state purposes.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal principle not discussed; adherents would answer by class interest.

individual-rights-only.rationale: MIM treats nations as real collective entities with rights to self-determination.

conscription.rationale: People's war envisions mass mobilization; mild inference.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit as a check on government is a libertarian idea alien to a revolutionary socialist programme; the sources do not discuss it.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marxist tradition stresses material conditions of freedom.

state-as-business.rationale: A proletarian state run on socialist lines is the opposite of treating citizens as customers, though the sources never address the idea.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents see the ruling class and state, not media and universities, as holding power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: MIM says race is a made-up idea used to justify oppression.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation conflicts with class politics.

total-state.rationale: Mixed; Maoist state directs a great deal, but this is not stated as a goal in the sources.

national-rebirth.rationale: Fascist-style rebirth is not a Maoist concern.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lin Biao condemns U.S. imperialism for 'armed aggression and suppression everywhere' and for subjecting Asia, Africa and Latin America to aggression and enslavement.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Maoism counts feudalism among the enemies of the national-democratic revolution, so feudal oaths of loyalty are clearly rejected, though not discussed in the sources.

bound-labor.rationale: Maoist revolution in the countryside aims to free peasants from landlord exploitation, so binding them to the land is rejected; the cited sources do not address it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: MIM treats ideology as class-based, pointing to the vantage point of the Third World proletariat; roughly Marxist standpoint view.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxist tradition treats morality as class-conditioned.

single-common-good.rationale: Class conflict, not unified common good, structures politics.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: MTW opposes settler colonialism and regards Israel as imperialism's outpost; the MIM sources read here do not address this directly.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Collective control of production, though not a distinct stated focus.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: opposed to market in public goods.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom for capital is seen as the basis of exploitation.

rule-by-example.rationale: Maoists rely on party discipline and state power, not moral example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: MIM states it supports the self-determination of all nations and peoples.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposition to imperialist force; the UN is also seen as imperialist-dominated, but adherents oppose unilateral Western force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Materialist tradition, though not mapped onto this statement.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: MIM treats closed borders and citizenship as keeping labor markets separate and a privilege of the First World; adherents lean against welfare chauvinism.

class-collaboration.rationale: MIM holds the labor aristocracy has an alliance with its capitalists, which it condemns.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Cultural Revolution's attack on old culture is upheld by MIM, but this statement about sacrificing institutions is unaddressed; slight lean.

dominated-front.rationale: Lin Biao calls for Asia, Africa and Latin America to encircle the imperialist powers; MTW centres a Third World front.

workers-nation.rationale: MIM insists on internationalism and rejects national-line organisation by First World workers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: MIM seeks to end oppression of genders, rejecting legally distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Neither Lin Biao nor MIM addresses usury laws; the Marxist critique targets surplus-value, not interest rates as such.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: MIM sees race as a made-up idea and opposes white-nation oppression.

state-class-instrument.rationale: MIM treats the US imperialist state as an instrument of class and national oppression.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism; extraction by oil firms is linked to imperialism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: No stated position; MIM opposes white-nation chauvinism.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim in contradiction with MIM's analysis of class and imperialism.

national-mission.rationale: Lin Biao makes support for revolutions abroad an internationalist duty, but as aid to other peoples' own wars against imperialism; a nation spreading its own government is the imperialism the tendency opposes.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: MIM aims to end oppression of genders, implying structural gender oppression.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Elites are viewed as serving the ruling class; broadly consistent.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: MIM Prisons targets state violence against oppressed nations.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A dictatorship of the proletariat directing the economy is far from a minimal state; implied by core principles rather than stated in the sources.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: MIM analyses oppression in terms of nations and imperialism and opposes white-nation chauvinism, which implies rejecting racial purity norms; the sources do not discuss intermarriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Strongly egalitarian aims, though MIM also treats First World workers as a non-revolutionary elite.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Maoism held socialism could be built in China; MIM says capitalist restoration remains possible; contested.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: MIM labels white nation as oppressor nation exploiting oppressed nations inside the US.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; MIM's focus on nations' self-determination cuts both ways on uniform personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not stated; Maoist states restricted religion but adherents mostly emphasise secularism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred as a religious-sentiment measure that a materialist, anti-religious tradition would not back.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Maoist state must stay strong and keep class struggle going; the sources read here do not state it as such.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Proletarian dictatorship over former rulers conflicts with a consent-only legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism not addressed; unequal exchange is attacked.

population-transfer.rationale: The tendency sides with oppressed nations against national oppression, which implies rejecting expulsion of minorities, though no source addresses it directly.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Lin Biao calls for armed people's wars in Asia, Africa and Latin America against imperialism and its lackeys, and makes supporting them an internationalist duty of socialist countries.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; adherents themselves are targeted.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-domination theme but not framed this way.

vanguard-party.rationale: MIM is a party applying democratic centralism and keeps a vanguard party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: MIM works from the vantage point of the Third World proletariat.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; MIM would see housing privatisation as a First World matter that does not touch exploitation.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: MIM sees First World strikes as alliance of white workers with monopoly capital but wouldn't back state limits.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: MIM and Maoism attribute poverty to imperialism and exploitation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Its framework treats conflict as rooted in imperialist exploitation, not ethnic diversity, so the claim is clearly rejected though not discussed as such.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; Maoists favour party selection and the mass line over either elections or sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would reject an imperialist state's suspension but defend proletarian dictatorship against enemies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Maoist states control the press; MIM sources read do not state this.

party-commands-army.rationale: Mao's principle that the party commands the gun.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from MIM's view that borders and citizenship divide labor markets; adherents would not endorse long waits.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Paris Commune principle in Marxist-Leninist tradition.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: MIM followed the democratic centralism of Leninist parties, under which adopted decisions bind members; the cited texts do not set this out.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: EU is an imperialist bloc in this analysis.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is incompatible with an atheist, materialist communist programme; no source discusses it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: MIM holds First World workers owe a debt to the Third World, and Lenin's revolutionary defeatism is part of MLM tradition.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Maoist tradition sets revolutionary criteria for art; mixed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Maoist parties set leadership by party line, not by term-limit rules.

recall-officials.rationale: Paris Commune tradition and Maoist mass line.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Opposes imperialist alliances and self-reliance is stressed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: collective housing is a socialist aim, but forced ownership by each family is not a Maoist goal.

people-in-arms.rationale: People's war with armed masses is central.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Maoist rural base focus is strategic, not moral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Maoism has a populist suspicion of intellectuals but not a clear one.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Adherents oppose white-nation chauvinism and ranking of peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; Maoist China used capital punishment, but MIM Prisons criticises the US system.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Dialectical materialism, which MIM upholds, rejects creationist teaching as idealism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; Maoist states restricted it, but MIM texts say nothing.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from MIM's internationalism and view of closed borders as a tool of First World privilege.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are materialist but defend oppressed nations against state repression, so split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A liberal Millian claim not addressed in the sources; the Maoist stress on collective discipline pulls against it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: MIM says a debt is owed to the Third World; cancellation of its debts follows.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Lin Biao says new democratic and socialist revolution is necessary, and MTW seeks delinking.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; Maoists prefer a new-democratic revolution led by the party over a liberal assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; Maoist states accepted such limits, but MTW texts focus on delinking instead.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: MIM says the First World owes a debt; aid framing differs (reparations).

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; Maoist China built its own bomb, but a First World deterrent is imperialist.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the question is a bourgeois-democratic institutional choice of no concern to MIM.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Socialist planning puts finance under the revolutionary state, so an independent price-stability central bank is ruled out by principle, not by any cited text.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from self-determination of oppressed nations.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Roughly right, but Maoism abolishes private property in means of production.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: MIM holds bourgeoisie seized power in USSR after Stalin, 1953, so Soviet Union later became capitalist, not wholly state-capitalist from start.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read, so adherents have no stated stance on environmental regulation under uncertainty.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Maoist tradition subordinates religious institutions to the socialist state; inferred as MIM texts say little.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: a head of state above class interest conflicts with the party-led proletarian dictatorship.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; adherents uphold self-determination, not special arrangements within larger states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Marxist materialism leaves no room for a ruler of divine descent; the sources simply never discuss sacred kingship.

character-from-environment.rationale: MIM says race is made-up and conditions form people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not addressed; Maoism subordinates the state to party line, not a ruler above law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read, and not a concern of a movement centred on Third World revolution.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Maoists see the state as one class's dictatorship over another, which rules out a balance of the few and the many; implied rather than stated.

leader-cult.rationale: Maoist history includes it but mixed.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; MIM's gender-equality aim gives no clear lean on custody courts.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: MIM states capitalist restoration can occur under party leaders and upholds the Cultural Revolution.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rely on peasants; land to the tiller in new democracy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nation is defined by land, so rejects ethno claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: A communist movement opposing religious authority would not punish leaving a religion; the sources are silent on apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: MIM treats gender oppression as a target of revolution, which implies rejecting mandatory covering, though no source mentions dress laws.

common-currency.rationale: Euro seen as imperialist bloc; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: MTW organises by class and imperialist oppression, not language-family or ancestry unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: MIM backs self-determination, not only autonomy; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; MIM's analysis of oppressed nations inside the US points to self-determination there, but is not a rule on emigration.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: It builds on historical materialism, though Maoism also stresses the active role of consciousness and the superstructure; the cited texts do not frame it this way.

ban-cartels.rationale: Monopoly capital not reformed, only overthrown.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; adherents see bailouts as capital's rescue by the imperialist state but no stated aim on policy.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: courts are class instruments, so adherents are indifferent between liberal limits and majority rule.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-reliance for Third World but not colonies.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Maoist people's war builds on mass base and rural bases rather than foco.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anti-feudal tradition of Maoism, in which new democracy ends landlord and hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; MIM's world-citizen internationalism gives no national-centred curriculum aim.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lin Biao treats colonial and semi-colonial rule over the peoples of the East as enslavement to be overthrown by anti-imperialist revolution, not as a stage of improvement.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from MIM's internationalism; members call themselves world citizens, not national patriots.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The tendency expects Third World revolutions to cut off the superprofits that sustain imperialism, implying capitalism cannot adapt its way out; the sources do not state this as such.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxism-Leninism-Maoism holds that class struggle, not competition between individuals or peoples, drives history, and MIM aims to end oppression of groups by groups.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from state economic management in socialist China; the sources read do not mention price controls.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: MIM's defining claim is that the First World working class is a bought-off labor aristocracy rather than part of the exploited proletariat.

delink-world-market.rationale: MTW calls for delinking Third World economies from the First World as part of global people's war.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist line of Lin Biao and MIM, which treats imperial influence over oppressed nations as exploitation to be ended.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: MIM treats private property rights as bourgeois and advocates state action against oppressor-nation privilege, so adherents reject a right to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: MIM regards bourgeois rights guarantees as class instruments and favours proletarian dictatorship over limits on it.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialism: imperialist-imposed borders and treaties are illegitimate to an oppressed-nations framework.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: MIM rejects bourgeois electoral politics and puts leadership in a vanguard party, not elected rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds the minority to the party line, so no minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of revolutionary war against reactionary rulers; the constitutional framing is not Maoist.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Lin Biao and MIM reject the parliamentary road as revisionist; power comes from people's war.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; a materialist, anti-capitalist outlook usually accepts animal sentience.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; humane use is the usual Marxist default.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine treats First World wealth as extracted surplus, so paternalist charity is not a duty but repayment is.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mass mobilisation and people's war require active political participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: MIM argues First World culture and consumption bind the labor aristocracy to imperialism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: MIM holds First World workers are bought off with imperialist superprofits, which is consent through material bribery.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Core thesis: First World wealth rests on surplus extracted from the Third World (dependency theory).

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: internationalist and anti-chauvinist, rejects citizenship-based privilege in the First World.

party-own-road.rationale: Lin Biao stresses each revolution is made independently and criticises revisionist direction by Moscow.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Lin Biao's chapter makes self-reliance the principle of revolution and construction, and MIM urges delinking.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: territorial revanchism reads as nationalism rather than class struggle, though oppressed-nation claims are supported.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: MIM treats settler nations as oppressors and backs leadership by oppressed and indigenous nations.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from opposition to fascism in the Comintern and Maoist tradition.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents defend the communist record and reject equating it with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: its settler-colonial and white-nation analysis puts slavery and racial oppression at the root of the US state.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: iconoclastic stance toward symbols of oppressors.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: MIM treats men of the First World as an exploiting group and rejects male-disadvantage framings.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from MIM's view of patriarchy as structural male oppression of women.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Maoist emphasis on each country's own path, not universal Western institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party commands the gun, so the army is a party instrument rather than an independent guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from Maoist socialist feminism that treats women's domestic labor as exploited.

filial-duty.rationale: Maoism attacked traditional hierarchy and Confucian family obligation; inferred, not addressed in the cited texts.

office-by-exam.rationale: Maoism favours the mass line and mass participation over credentialed bureaucratic elites; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Lin Biao's text calls for oppressed nations to break imperialist control of their economies, which supports blocking foreign takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Maoist tradition promoted free divorce (the 1950 PRC marriage law); inferred as the strand's view.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Maoists cite the Paris Commune model of recallable delegates; inferred from that tradition.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatised pensions are the opposite of a collective, state-run provision; MIM rejects market solutions. Inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land to the tiller and collective ownership are core to Maoist rural revolution; inferred for the communal-tenure claim.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: MIM treats bourgeois parliaments as instruments of the labour aristocracy and rejects electoral politics; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Self-determination for oppressed nations is central, so enforced single-language states are inferred as opposed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Anti-imperialist control of national resources implies barring foreign land ownership; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: MIM treats racial and national oppression as structural and denies it depends on intent; inferred for this statement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: MIM argues First World workers are bought off with consumption bought by Third World exploitation, so consumerism is treated as harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Lin Biao's text calls for support of people's wars abroad; here inferred as backing for insurgents against hostile governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-hegemonism rejects great-power control over other states; inferred, since the cited texts predate the key cases.

corporate-influence.rationale: Maoist analysis treats the state as serving imperialist capital; the criticism is inferred, not stated on lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Anti-imperialism of Lin Biao and MIM favours Third World states shielding themselves from imperialist penetration; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Texts here do not address population policy and adherents are not documented either way.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear position can be inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Socialist construction implies guaranteed employment; inferred from MIM’s approach to proletarian welfare.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lin Biao and MIM see the imperialist democracies as exploiter powers that wage wars of plunder, not as peaceful.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Maoism-Third Worldism treats law as the instrument of the ruling class, but a committed adherent also wants socialist legality after revolution; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Global people’s war supports revolutionary struggle across borders, though it opposes imperialist intervention; the absolute statement is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist organising of the proletariat; not stated in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: MIM was an anti-racist movement that blamed imperialism and its labor aristocracy, not a minority; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the family is treated as part of socialist reconstruction and no abolition position is documented.

public-access-to-information.rationale: No documented position; a Leninist party values secrecy but also mass publicity.

local-production.rationale: Delinking from the First World implies self-reliant Third World production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: MIM held that a Leninist vanguard party is essential to lead people’s war.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Both international and bourgeois national law are seen as instruments of imperialism; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Marxist-Leninist-Maoist materialism rejects religion as a basis of the nation; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Lin Biao frames the struggle against imperialist hegemony as one of oppressed nations asserting independence, so ritual deference to a leading power is rejected (inferred).

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: MIM treats the world economy as extraction from the Third World and favours redistribution by need, so keeping regional revenue is inferred to be opposed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Standard Marxist-Leninist-Maoist doctrine abolishes private ownership of the means of production while leaving personal belongings alone.

defeat-communism.rationale: Maoism-Third Worldism is itself a communist current aiming at global communism through people's war.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Socialist construction places services under state ownership and control; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from classical Marxist-Leninist treatment of religion as opium; MIM texts opened do not address it directly.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxists credit capitalism with creating productive power, but MIM calls First World capitalism parasitic and exploitative; no clear single line (inferred).

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist tradition and Maoist stress on women's liberation as part of socialist transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialist construction in the Maoist tradition collectivised domestic work through public services; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: internationalist Maoism does not prize linguistic purity, which is a nationalist concern.

treaties-binding.rationale: MIM backed self-determination of oppressed nations inside the US, so treaties with them are inferred to be upheld.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mao's rural people's communes are the model for collective rural life, though under party direction; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: MIM opposes settler colonialism and national oppression, so state-promoted majority settlement in minority regions is inferred to be opposed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Maoism holds communism, reached through people's war, to be the sound basis for society, and rejects a third way as revisionism.

missingStatements.text: Workers in rich countries are mostly not exploited, and share in the profits that rich countries extract from poor ones.
missingStatements.rationale: MIM's defining claim is that the First World working class is a bought-off labor aristocracy rather than part of the exploited proletariat.

missingStatements.text: Poor countries should break their economic ties with rich countries rather than seek integration into the world market.
missingStatements.rationale: MTW calls for delinking Third World economies from the First World as part of global people's war.

missingStatements.text: The decisive revolutionary struggles of our era are those of the peoples of Asia, Africa and Latin America rather than the workers of rich countries.
missingStatements.rationale: Lin Biao presents the Third World as the world's countryside whose struggles decide world revolution.
missingStatements.declined: Too specific to this ideology to be a lean, widely contestable statement; its core is covered by the new labor-aristocracy statement and by dominated-front.

notes: MTW is a small, mostly US-based current; Wikipedia says proponents dispute details such as the joint-dictatorship of oppressed nations' proletariat. Many answers are inferred from MIM and Maoist tradition and marked low; the high and medium answers are those on class, imperialism, nations, party and revolution.
